newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer eyes sales topping 50 bln dmk in 97.
newsitem.headline: Bayer eyes sales topping 50 bln dmk in 97.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG said on Tuesday it planned to post sales of 50 billion marks ($29.6 billion) or more and keep its profits at record levels this year.

"For 1997 we have set ourselves the goal of exceeding 50 billion marks in sales for the first time. The prospects are particulalry bright in the pharmaceuticals, plastics, crop protection, diagnostics and animal health divisions," Bayer said in its annual report.
At the same time Bayer also expects to post very strong profits, predicting "we will at least repeat last year's strong performances, and improve on it if possible."

For 1996, Bayer, long considered the steadiest and strongest earner among Germany's three leading chemicals and drugs group which also include Hoechst AG and BASF AG, posted a pre-tax profit of 4.46 billion marks and sales of 48.6 billion marks.

Bayer, which has shied away from spectacular takeovers in the past preferring to make smaller acquisitions instead, said "we will also continue to strengthen our market positions throuh selective acquisitions and alliances."
The group said that 1997 began "according to plan" declining to be more specific however.

Generally Bayer, like its competitors, is betting on improved global economic conditions to give its own business a boost. The group expects this will lead to higher volume sales even though increased international competition may leave little room for price adjustments.

Stiff international competition will also force Bayer to stick to its cost-cutting programmes which mean "further reductions in thze workforce will unfortunately be inevitable in areas that are not sufficiently profitable."

After grappling with the negative effects of a very strong mark in 1995, Bayer predicted that conditions would remain positive in 1997, after improving in 1996. "With the value of most currencies increaseing against the mark in 1996, we are expecting that exchange rates will again have a positive effect on sales and earnings in 1997."
In order to growth this year, Bayer said it had raised its capital expenditure and research budgets for 1997 to a total of 7.8 billion marks.
